summary: Maries County towersite acquired 1948-49; steel tower erected 1970-71. MDC now runs the area and says the tower's stairs are open to visitors.

access.note: MDC conservation area. Visitors can use the stairs; the highest portions are blocked off for safety.

visit.trail_note: Stairs only; the highest portions are closed.

facts.agency: Missouri Conservation Commission (later Missouri Department of Conservation)

events.note: In the 1950s the tower was used as a Ground Observer Corps observation post. The page gives no exact year.
FY 1958-59: the wooden fire tower cab was completely remodeled.
FY 1970-71: a steel lookout tower was erected. The page does not say whether it replaced the wooden tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1948-49 report gives a 10-acre towersite. MDC lists 11.8 total acres, and Wikipedia gives 12. The figures differ slightly; no source explains why.

notes_for_editor: The 1970-71 steel tower and the historic fire tower the MDC page describes may or may not be the same structure; the MDC page gives no date, so the link is not confirmed. The brief lists the agency as Missouri Conservation Commission, which was the name in the 1948-49 and 1958-59 reports; later sources use the Department of Conservation. Brief status was unknown; the MDC page's present tense supports standing. Story is about 180 words. Checked 2026-10-21: the MDC page does not mention 1970 or steel, so the link between the 1970-71 steel tower and the historic fire tower is unconfirmed. The story now says so and no longer implies they are the same structure.
